post.caption: The Armada Jewel postdates the Armada. It is a gold locket made around 1600, and its Armada name is a later popular title. The front shows Elizabeth I in gold, under rock crystal. It is set with diamonds and rubies. A miniature of the queen inside was painted by Nicholas Hilliard. The back shows the English Church as an ark on stormy seas, and its Latin motto speaks of calm through fierce waves. Tradition says Elizabeth I gave it to Sir Thomas Heneage. The V&A says there is no evidence for that story. It reached the V&A in 1935 after a Christie's auction.
